reviews.title: Two years later and it's still a good monitor to buy
reviews.comment: I've been using this monitor for two years now and it was purchased specifically for its size, features, and stellar reviews even at the time. The fact that there are still recent purchases with equally satisfied customers I think speaks volume for it. I actually do not use it for gaming (or at least not currently), but rather as a monitor for an Apple TV setup. I needed a VERY specific size to fit a confined space on the wall and it is exactly the largest I could have fit. 25" diagonal is not a common size and the low profile bezel is very nice. So two thumbs up for Samsung having accurate dimensions listed. It also attached perfectly to my mount if that is of any concern. No, it does not have speakers, but it does pass through audio via a 1/8" out and it works perfectly. You could also use an HDMI audio extractor if you need to pull a higher quality from your source. The picture quality from my Apple TV is excellent with absolutely no jitter, excellent color reproduction, and is very sharp. This isn't an expensive monitor with more bells and whistles, is "only" 1080p, and isn't my 65" OLED tv, but for the price and excellent user satisfaction I really think it hits the mark. Gamers seem to be very satisfied, and if it's doing a good job at rendering their games to their standards then I knew my basic usage was going to be good.

reviews.title: More than enough for gaming
reviews.comment: ’ve been using the Samsung Odyssey G4 25″ gaming monitor for a few weeks now, and overall it’s been a very impressive display, especially for fast-paced gaming. Performance: This monitor is very smooth. The 240 Hz refresh rate combined with a 1 ms response time makes motion feel fluid and crisp — perfect for competitive shooters, racing games, or any title where input speed and clarity during rapid movement matter. There’s very little motion blur, even when things get hectic on screen. Visuals: The FHD (1080p) resolution on a 25″ screen looks clear and sharp for most use cases. The IPS panel means colors are vibrant and viewing angles are wide — side-by-side games and videos look consistently good even if you’re not sitting perfectly center. It’s not a 4K panel, but for gaming this size/resolution hits a great balance of performance and graphical clarity. Adaptive Sync & Compatibility: I tested it with both G-Sync Compatible on my NVIDIA GPU and Adaptive Sync on AMD, and the experience was smooth — fewer tears or stutters compared to V-Sync-only setups. If you’re into esports titles or any competitive gaming, this is where the panel really shines. Build & Features: The design is fairly minimal but gaming-friendly — slim bezels and a clean stand that doesn’t take up too much desk space. The OSD menu is intuitive, and setting up presets for different game genres is quick. A couple of things to note: The resolution is 1080p, which is great for high frame-rate gaming, but if you prefer really detailed visuals for single-player games or creative work, a higher-res panel (1440p+) might feel sharper. It doesn’t have integrated speakers, so you’ll need separate audio if you want sound from your setup. Overall: This Samsung Odyssey G4 monitor delivers excellent performance for gamers, particularly if you care about refresh rate and responsiveness. The IPS panel keeps colors nice, and the adaptive sync support makes gameplay feel smooth. If your priority is competitive gaming and fast visuals without sacrificing quality, this monitor is a strong choice at its price point.
